text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope. Given the classic presentation of syncope immediately following urination in an older male, with a normal ECG and no reported prodromal symptoms like chest pain or palpitations, the most likely cause is vasovagal syncope triggered by the Valsalva maneuver and subsequent vasodilation during micturition. While we have ruled out the most dangerous cardiac causes with the initial tests, if the patient had a known history of aortic stenosis, this would be a medical emergency until proven otherwise. Since you have regained consciousness without confusion, this is consistent with a benign etiology. We will monitor you briefly to ensure stability before discharge.
